a_measurement_error_i_made_and_corrected.also_briefly_suspected: a file appearing and disappearing between runs, since rglob returned 40 once and 41 twice. It was the same basename collision in a set, not a writer; no process held the worktree.
a_measurement_error_i_made_and_corrected.fix: Every index is keyed by the path below the evidence root, and record_key() says why.
a_measurement_error_i_made_and_corrected.the_bug: I keyed the catalogue by basename. Two records share the filename ordinary-window-audit.json, so a name-keyed index holds 40 entries for 41 files and silently drops one. The first version of the coverage test asserted a count of 41 against that set of 40 and failed.
a_measurement_error_i_made_and_corrected.what_i_first_reported_to_myself: 41 records, 26 covered by invariants, against a set of 40
a_measurement_error_i_made_and_corrected.why_it_mattered_beyond_the_count: The figure-binding table was also name-keyed, so one record was invisible to it and a figure held only by the shadowed copy could have been reported as uniquely binding a different record.

design_constraint.adopted: Every check derives what it expects from something outside the record: the bytes of a file the record names, a figure another file cites, or an invariant implied by the field's own name.
design_constraint.rejected: asserting each record's contents against a hardcoded copy in the test
design_constraint.why: That doubles every figure and makes the test the thing that drifts. It is the defect this lane fixed in #1004, not a fix for it.

how_the_gap_was_found.reproduced_here: yes, independently, before writing anything: the same corruption applied to band-validity-sweep.json left test_open3d.py and test_open3d_lineage.py at 120 passed
how_the_gap_was_found.their_demonstration: corrupted eight records in place, every boolean flipped and every number negated, and all 120 executing tests still passed
how_the_gap_was_found.why_mentions_were_not_enough: Four records are cited by name in test_open3d.py docstrings and more in skills/tools/open3d/SKILL.md, but a citation in prose is read by people, not by CI.

how_the_vocabulary_was_widened.one_candidate_measured_and_rejected: Lowering the citation threshold from four decimals to three would have added 2 bindings, both to a record already pinned, against 23 newly ambiguous figures. Measured and dropped rather than adopted for the coverage it appeared to offer.

two_candidate_rules_that_were_wrong_and_.cells_as_a_count: _cells$ as a count rule fails on correct data too: recall_of_observed_cells is a rate of 0.96, not a count. The proportion test runs first, which is why both are now right.
two_candidate_rules_that_were_wrong_and_.how_they_were_found: By measuring each candidate rule against the committed catalogue before adopting it, not by reading the field names. Each rejected correct data on the first attempt.
two_candidate_rules_that_were_wrong_and_.recall_as_a_proportion: ^recall as a [0, 1] rule fails on correct data: recall_delta is -0.0016, a genuine negative difference. Deltas became their own class.

what_was_added.delta: recall_delta and siblings, which live in [-1, 1] rather than [0, 1]
what_was_added.fit_ratio: a path rule, not a name rule: the viewer capability record keys its fit ratios by human view names like "Observed scan only", which no field-name pattern can reach
what_was_added.proportion: _rate$, ^recall_of, ^precision_ -- what the occupancy records call their numbers

how_the_vocabulary_was_widened.why: The first version of this guard reached 27 of 42 records and left 13 with structural checks only. Among those 13 were both downstream-consumer records and a capability record -- the lane's actual consumer evidence, and the records review said were worth the most. They were not inherently uncheckable; the field-name rules were too narrow.

the_control_that_shows_the_widening_matt.a_first_attempt_at_this_control_that_was: Running the old guard against the *new* record made it fail on its two coverage tests, which looked like detection and was only the schema having changed underneath it. The control is only informative with both halves from the same commit.
the_control_that_shows_the_widening_matt.previous_guard_baseline: 10 passed, agreeing with the record of its own commit
the_control_that_shows_the_widening_matt.previous_guard_on_the_corruption: 10 passed -- it detects none of it
the_control_that_shows_the_widening_matt.what_was_run: The previous committed guard and the previous committed coverage record, both restored from the earlier commit so the comparison is not confounded by the schema change, then the same two records corrupted.

mutations_the_guard_was_tested_against.why_figures_here_are_written_as_text: Mutation 2 moves a fraction that test_open3d.py quotes. Recording the before and after as numbers would put that figure in a second record, making it ambiguous and so silently removing the binding this record exists to document. The harness recomputes both values on every run.
mutations_the_guard_was_tested_against.why_there_is_no_count_field: There was one, and it said 9 against the 13 results beside it. Nothing read it -- the guard binds len(results) -- so it drifted, which is the exact defect this record exists to catch, sitting inside the record. A reviewer found it. Deleted rather than given a second reader: len(results) is already authoritative and already bound, and a field whose only job is to restate a length it cannot see is the thing this pull request argues against.

a_duplicated_record.action_taken: Held equal by a test rather than deleted. Both are committed evidence and the ambiguous reference does not establish which copy is meant; divergence is the failure worth catching, and that is now caught.
a_duplicated_record.finding: ordinary-window-audit.json is committed twice, at the top level and under viewer-ui/, byte for byte identical, and README.md refers to it by bare filename without saying which.
a_duplicated_record.left_for_review: whether one copy should go, and which

three_docstring_citations_that_do_not_ho.action_taken: Recorded, not edited. test_open3d.py is touched by several open PRs in this lane and a prose-only correction there would conflict for no functional gain.
three_docstring_citations_that_do_not_ho.consequence_for_the_guard: This is why the figure binding is derived from the data rather than taken from the docstring's citation. A figure sourced from elsewhere falls out of scope instead of producing a false failure.
three_docstring_citations_that_do_not_ho.finding: Three figures in test_open3d.py docstrings that name an evidence record are not in the record they name. 1.5 is a descriptor (voxels wide), and 0.75126 is attributed in the prose itself to another lane's construction; floor-vs-voxel-multiple.json holds 0.7503 and 0.7536, not 0.75126.
three_docstring_citations_that_do_not_ho.left_for_review: whether those three docstrings should be reworded to separate their own figures from quoted ones

verification.existing_open3d_suites_rerun: test_open3d.py and test_open3d_lineage.py unchanged and passing
verification.guard_imports_no_product_code: deliberate. It reads files by path from a root derived from __file__, so it cannot resolve to another worktree's copy of the package the way an imported threshold did in #1004.
verification.lint: ruff check and ruff format clean
verification.why_there_is_no_test_count: There was one, and it said '9 passed' against 12 tests collected. A test count is reproducible on demand and goes stale every time a test is added, so it is recorded nowhere now. The suites above are named instead, which is the part a reader cannot regenerate.

a_migration_this_sweep_found_and_the_fix.measured_effect: Under the type-respecting edit, 16 records resisted before the fix and 18 after. Review measured 24 unnoticed with an independently written sweep, which is exactly what this one measured before the fix.
a_migration_this_sweep_found_and_the_fix.the_defect: Before this measurement, a type-respecting edit to capability-record-distance-bands.json was unnoticed even though eleven citations pinned it. The edit destroyed all eleven of its bindings and created eleven new ones against other records: deleting one occurrence of a figure that appeared in two records makes it unique in the other, and so newly bindable under the exactly-one-record rule. The published total stayed at 29, the recomputation test passed, and a record pinned by eleven citations became pinned by none.
a_migration_this_sweep_found_and_the_fix.the_fix: The coverage block now publishes figure_bindings_by_record, recomputed by the same test. The migration now fails it.
a_migration_this_sweep_found_and_the_fix.why_it_got_through: figure_bindings_derived is a count over a derived set, and a count is blind to membership moving. Eleven lost and eleven gained nets to zero.

what_a_believable_edit_actually_resists.the_two_modes_and_why_the_difference_mat: A naive sweep multiplies every number by 1.03 and keeps proportions in [0, 1]. It is caught in 31 of 40 records -- and it flatters the guard, because a count of 42 becomes 43.26 and the count invariant rejects that for not being an integer. Detecting a type error is not detecting a plausible re-measurement; nobody publishes 43.26 harnesses. The type-respecting mode moves a proportion within [0, 1], a count to a neighbouring integer, and a delta within [-1, 1], so every value stays something the record could legitimately have held.
what_a_believable_edit_actually_resists.what_this_means_for_the_claim: 18 of 40 records resist an edit that keeps every value legitimate. 7 of those resist because a figure in them is quoted in code or prose outside the record; the other 11 resist through a different cross-check, such as the duplicated filename held equal to its twin or this record's own recomputation. The remaining 22 are the floor of a range-invariant mechanism, not an oversight. Review's phrasing was that the resistance comes from the citation-pinned records rather than the invariant-covered ones; that is the right direction and it is incomplete, because 11 of the 18 come from neither.
what_a_believable_edit_actually_resists.why_this_is_here: Acceptance criterion 2 was that a believable edit -- one cited fraction re-measured by a few percent, still finite, still in range -- fails a test. That was demonstrated on one record and it holds. Review then quantified it across the catalogue and found most records do not resist such an edit. That is not a contradiction of anything published here: a range invariant cannot detect an in-range value, by construction. The useful statement is which mechanism carries the resistance, so it is measured rather than asserted.

what_is_still_unguarded.honest_summary: 40 of 42 records now carry a check that means something about the values inside them. The catalogue is not self-verifying and these tests do not re-run any geometry; they hold the committed records to their own arithmetic and to the files and prose that cite them.
what_is_still_unguarded.the_hole_this_leaves: Those two records can be rewritten to anything plausible and only parsing, non-emptiness and finite numbers will object.
what_is_still_unguarded.why_it_is_not_closed_with_a_digest_manif: A manifest over all 42 would detect every change including every legitimate regeneration, so it reports edits rather than errors. It is the right instrument if review wants acknowledge-on-change, and it is a different decision from this one.
what_is_still_unguarded.why_these_two_and_not_others: Neither contains a single number. live-runtime-attempt.json and viewer-ui/ordinary-native-capture-status.json are entirely prose and booleans, so there is no quantity for a range or sign rule to hold and no figure for code or prose to quote. That is a floor, not an oversight: the only instruments left for them are a byte digest or a schema the catalogue does not share.

what_this_records: The Open3D evidence catalogue had no reader. 41 committed records, and no test, script or workflow opened one of them. This records the guard added in answer, what it covers, what it does not, and the mutations proving it fails when a record is wrong.
why_the_coverage_figures_moved_by_one: Deleting the stale `count` field removed one integer from the swept population, so the record's own coverage figures moved with it: 40 records to 39, 1093 values to 1092, and the `count` invariant from 143 to 142. These are published and bound, so the guard failed until they were updated -- which is the behaviour the two deleted fields did not have.
